workLog.step: Measured the #3747 premise before acting on it
workLog.detail: The issue reports one bypass: demoting a required MUST to SHOULD. Scanned all 1,027 committed logs. 257 demotions exist and every one already carries evidence, so the named bypass has never been used. A second, unnamed bypass is wide open: 138 required items declare no level key at all. Because every check in validate_must_item is gated on level == 'MUST', an absent level skips all of them. The absent-level hole covers branchVerified 19 times and notOnMain 4 times, the two items that answer whether the session ran on main.

workLog.step: Closed both holes with one flag
workLog.detail: Threaded an is_required flag from validate_checklist_section into validate_must_item. A required item with no level is now an error. A required item demoted below MUST while incomplete and carrying no evidence is now an error, which enforces SESSION-PROTOCOL.md line 20 as written rather than inventing policy. Demotion itself stays legal because Copilot CLI exposes no Serena tools and pinning serenaActivated to MUST would invalidate every Copilot session.
count_must_failures matches on exact prefixes, so an unregistered MUST-level message is one CI silently never counts. Issue #3365 was exactly this drift, and a test now pins the registration.

workLog.step: Made the schema name every root field the protocol requires
workLog.detail: SESSION-PROTOCOL.md line 946 lists six required root fields and build_session_log emits all six, but the schema named two. Promoted schemaVersion, workLog, endingCommit and nextSteps to required. The schema was the only one of the three documents disagreeing with the other two.

Promoting the four fields initially broke renames of historical logs, which is the exact regression #3385 fixed. Threaded existing_log into validate_against_schema and subtracted precisely those four names from the root required list in record mode. A rename cannot supply a workLog the session never wrote, and fabricating one to clear a gate is the behaviour that issue forbids. Two mutants pin the subtraction to exactly four names.

workLog.step: Verified both rules ratchet practice rather than change it
workLog.detail: The last log missing a level is dated 2026-03-09; the most recent 397 logs have none. build_session_log emits level on all twelve required items and all six root fields, so a freshly generated log trips neither rule. A test asserts this against the real generator so the claim is checked, not remembered.

16-mutant harness: suppress each new error, remove the is_required guard, cut the call-site wiring, drop each exemption, accept whitespace as justification, unregister the prefixes, remove the relaxation, apply it unconditionally, cut the existing_log threading, and drop each of the five required entries individually. All 16 caught, 0 survived.
